title: AI-Assisted WES Variant Interpretation in Neurodevelopmental Disorders: A Narrative Review of Existing Tools.
authors: Treccarichi, Simone; Vinci, Mirella; Musumeci, Antonino; Galati Rando, Rosanna; Fallea, Antonio; Brancato, Desiree; Bruno, Francesca; Federico, Concetta; Saccone, Salvatore; Elia, Maurizio; Cali, Francesco
one_liner_zh: 该文是神经发育障碍中WES变异解读的AI工具综述，仅将蛋白结构预测作为辅助环节提及，核心为临床基因组变异解读，不涉及蛋白质结构计算建模的方法创新。
abstract: Background/Objectives: Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) comprise a heterogeneous group of conditions characterized by alterations in brain development and function, frequently associated with complex genetic architectures. The widespread implementation of next-generation sequencing, particularly whole-exome sequencing (WES), has substantially increased the identification of potentially disease-associated variants, shifting the major challenge from variant detection to their interpretation and prioritization. This review examines the emerging contribution of artificial intelligence (AI) to WES variant interpretation in NDDs, with particular emphasis on AI-assisted variant prioritization and protein structural modelling. Methods: We reviewed conventional computational and emerging AI-driven approaches applicable to different stages of WES interpretation, including variant pathogenicity and functional-effect prediction, evolutionary conservation, splicing assessment, phenotype-informed prioritization, and protein structure prediction. Their methodological principles, applications, and major limitations were critically examined within the context of neurodevelopmental genomics. Results: AI and machine-learning approaches increasingly integrate genomic, phenotypic, functional, and structural information, supporting phenotype-aware candidate prioritization and molecular contextualization of selected variants. However, computational outputs are affected by model-specific limitations and should not be considered independent evidence of pathogenicity. Their added value depends primarily on the complementarity and biological relevance of the information provided, rather than on predictor concordance alone. Conclusions: This narrative review highlights that AI-assisted WES interpretation should prioritize complementary, mechanism-relevant evidence over computational concordance. AI-assisted tools should therefore be selected according to variant class and disease mechanism and integrated with independent clinical, genetic, and functional evidence.
abstract_zh: 背景/目标：神经发育障碍（NDDs）包括一组异质性疾病，其特征为脑发育和功能改变，常与复杂的遗传结构相关。下一代测序，尤其是全外显子组测序（WES）的广泛实施，大幅增加了潜在疾病相关变异的识别，使主要挑战从变异检测转向其解读和优先级排序。本综述探讨了人工智能（AI）在NDDs的WES变异解读中新兴的贡献，尤其侧重于AI辅助的变异优先级排序和蛋白质结构建模。方法：我们综述了适用于WES解读不同阶段的传统计算方法和新兴AI驱动方法，包括变异致病性和功能效应预测、进化保守性、剪接评估、表型信息指导的优先级排序以及蛋白质结构预测。在神经发育基因组学背景下，对其方法学原理、应用和主要局限性进行了批判性审视。结果：AI和机器学习方法日益整合基因组、表型、功能和结构信息，支持表型感知的候选变异优先级排序和所选变异的分子背景化。然而，计算输出受模型特定局限性的影响，不应被视为致病性的独立证据。其附加价值主要取决于所提供信息的互补性和生物学相关性，而非仅取决于预测因子的一致性。结论：本叙述性综述强调，AI辅助的WES解读应优先考虑互补的、机制相关的证据，而非计算一致性。因此，AI辅助工具应根据变异类别和疾病机制进行选择，并与独立的临床、遗传和功能证据相结合。
